## About This Project

ALIGATEHR-Gen (ALIgning Graph Attention neTworks for EHR using Genetic kinship) is a deep learning framework that integrates electronic health records (EHR), genetic data, and external medical ontology knowledge into an attention-based predictive model. By leveraging genetically inferred first-degree relationships, ALIGATEHR-Gen addresses the underutilization of family health history in disease risk prediction, where such information is often missing or incomplete in clinical records.

Our model constructs unified patient representations by incorporating genetically inferred first-degree relationships and disease ontology embeddings. Evaluated on **118 diseases** across the UK Biobank, ALIGATEHR-Gen outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models by an average of at least **6% in AUC**.

## Key Highlights

<div class="card-grid">

<div class="card">

### Graph Attention Network

The first attention-based GNN model that integrates clinical features and genetic data for disease risk prediction, using genetically inferred first-degree relationships as graph edges.

</div>

<div class="card">

### Multimodal Data Integration

Integrates multimodal patient data including genetic information, diagnosis codes, demographics, along with external medical ontology knowledge for enhanced patient representation.

</div>

<div class="card">

### Superior Predictive Performance

Achieves an average AUC of **0.76** across 118 diseases, outperforming five baseline models including Logistic Regression, XGBoost, RNN, Dipole, and GRAM.

</div>

</div>

## Case Study: Fibrotic Diseases

A case study on five primary fibrotic and closely related diseases — coronary artery disease (CAD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), pulmonary fibrosis (PF), and Crohn's disease (CD) — reveals that ALIGATEHR-Gen effectively distinguishes patient subgroups based on clinical and genetic features. High-risk patients consistently have a greater number of affected family members and elevated BMI, demonstrating the model's capacity to capture interactions between genetic factors, demographics, and clinical features.
